messages.subject: Re: Lines scale_color_gradient, points scale_color_discrete
parts:
Hi:

Anyone who uses dput() deserves a response :) This isn't the most aesthetically pleasing suggestion, but here goes...

I decided to plot the indicator for decay as a size aesthetic, but you've got to be a little bit clever. What I did was to define the desired point sizes as levels of a new factor, call it in geom_point() as a size aesthetic and then try to get the scale right at the end. Here's the code:

# Create a new factor decay with the desired point sizes
# (2, 4.5 - you might want to change it...)
DFD.weight <- transform(DFD.weight, decay = factor(2 + 2.5 * Decay))

# Use the new factor as a size aesthetic in geom_point() and use
# scale_size_manual() to get the right discrete point sizes and labels

DFD.graph<-ggplot(data=DFD.weight, aes(Day, Weight, group=Fruit)) +
geom_line(aes(color=Ripeness))+
geom_point(aes(shape = factor(Fruit), size = decay)) +

scale_y_continuous('Fruit Weight (g)')+
scale_x_continuous('Days')+
scale_shape('Fruit')+
scale_color_gradient('Ripening Stage', low='green', high='red')+

scale_size_manual('Decay', breaks = c(2, 4.5), values = c(2, 4.5),
                  labels = c('No', 'Yes')) +

facet_wrap(~ Genotype)+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black", vjust=1),
     axis.text.y = theme_text(colour="black", hjust=1))

DFD.graph

Only 9 of the 224 observations exhibited decay, and you have to look carefully to find the +'s that correspond. If you like the idea, you might want to choose shapes that will show size differences more easily. The filled squares show up easily enough :), but in Genotype F2, there are three fruit type 13 observations that exhibit decay which are difficult to see because of the choice of shape (+). One idea might be to use unfilled shapes for the non-decayed fruit and filled shapes for the decayed fruit. Look into the values option for scale_shape to specify these.

I'm wondering about the effectiveness of ripening stage as a color gradient for lines. Visually, all I can see are the middle and extremes - you might want to consider combining stages into perhaps a three-level factor instead (?) Just a thought...

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Lines scale_color_gradient, points scale_color_discrete
parts:
Dennis, 

Thanks for the response, I got distracted from my graphing by a conference. 

I went with the point size and simply plotted it as a factor between 0 and 1. The size difference is fine using the embedded defaults (Kudos to Hadley for that). 

I also went with your idea and used scale_color_gradient2() and defined the midpoint as yellow. This actually works really well since it mimicks the color of the tomato fruit pretty darn closely. 

DFD.graph<-ggplot(data=DFD.weight, aes(Day, Percent.Loss, group=Fruit)) +

geom_line(aes(color=Ripeness))+

geom_point(aes(shape = factor(Fruit), size=factor(Decay)))+

scale_y_continuous('Weight Loss (%)')+

scale_x_continuous('Days')+

scale_shape('Fruit')+

scale_color_gradient2('Ripening Stage', low='green',mid='yellow', high='red',midpoint=4)+

scale_size_discrete('Decay', label=c('No', 'Yes'), breaks=c("0","1"))+

facet_wrap(~ Genotype)+ 

opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black", vjust=1)

, axis.text.y = theme_text(colour="black", hjust=1))

DFD.graph

I take it that it's not possible to have two color scales, one for lines and one for points. I have another factor that I'd like to plot against (Wrinkle) that has 11 values (1-10). I'd like to keep the gradient scale for the line so you can see how each fruit it maturing and then have another scale for the points so you can see how decayed or wrinkly they are. Or am I putting to much information on one graph?

Brandon

different subsets of the data.
